title: Ops Trust Network Playbook: 30-120 Day Roadmap
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a working playbook for creating an "ops trust network" — a lightweight, cross-functional program to operationalize reliability targets (SLOs) and make fast, repeatable decisions when services hit error budgets or latency regressions. Goal is to reduce mean time to mitigation for reliability incidents while increasing shared ownership and predictable rollout of SLOs across platform and product teams.

Audience:
- Platform engineering leads (primary)
- Feature/product engineers and PMs
- SRE/stability partners
- Solutions & customer-facing eng for high-risk customers

High-level approach (why this is different):
- Networked guardians: pair a platform engineer + feature owner as "service guardians" for the first 90 days after an SLO is adopted.
- Short, measurable experiments (30/60/90/120 day cadence) instead of big-bang SLO rollout.
- Runbook-first: every SLO must have a 1‑page mitigation play (invocation steps, temporary mitigations, telemetry to check).
- Error budget policy as code: automated enforcement + human-reviewed exemptions via a simple triage flow.

30/60/90/120 day plan (sprint-matrix style):
- Days 0–30 (Pilot & discover):
  - Select 3 pilot services: one low-risk infra service, one internal product service, one customer-facing inference route.
  - Define candidate SLOs (availability, p95 latency, quality check counts) and baseline metrics.
  - Create 1‑page runbooks and add to repo: ops/playbooks/pilot-<service>.md.
  - Weekly "trust network" sync (30m) for pilots; ad-hoc Slack channel for rapid triage.
  - Success signals: runbooks exist, telemetry dashboards created, owners assigned.

- Days 31–60 (Iterate & automate):
  - Automate basic alerts (error budget burn > 25%/24h) and a quick triage checklist in PagerDuty.
  - Implement error budget policy gating in CI for non-critical rollouts (block feature flags if error budget > threshold).
  - Run 2 tabletop exercises simulated on pilot services.
  - Docs: onboarding checklist for new guardians.
  - Success signals: alert noise reduced (target: <= 2 noisy false positives/week across pilots), CI gating exercised.

- Days 61–90 (Scale & institutionalize):
  - Expand the program to 8 services, onboard 6 guardian pairs.
  - Introduce SLO shadowing: feature teams mirror platform SLO signals for 2 weeks before adoption.
  - Introduce a playbook template and a lightweight SLA-to-SLO translation guide for PMs.
  - Success signals: average time-to-mitigation improved by 30% across onboarded services; guardianship rota in calendar.

- Days 91–120 (Policy & handoff):
  - Finalize error budget escalation policy: auto-threshold actions, cross-team escalation steps, and customer communication templates.
  - Create an "oncall mini-runway" for new services: 14-day shadow oncall pairing.
  - Begin monthly reliability review: 1 pager per service, decision log on whether SLOs change.
  - Success signals: program checklist green for 75% of services; decision log capturing roll/rollback reasons.

Roles and responsibilities (practical):
- Service Guardian (platform + feature): maintain runbook, run table-top, lead mitigation for the service during adoption.
- Reliability Coach (platform): run monthly reviews, maintain playbook templates, tidy signals and dashboards.
- Product Owner / PM: weigh in on cost/quality tradeoffs and approve SLO targets for customers.
- SRE Ops: implement CI gating and automated actions, own escalation hops.

Concrete artifacts to produce (minimal viable set):
- One-page runbook template (invocation steps, rollback quick wins, telemetry links).
- SLO definition template (objective, target, measurement window, exclusion rules).
- Error budget policy file (YAML) + example CI check.
- Triage checklist for first 60 minutes and first 24 hours.
- Workspace: slack #ops-trust-pilot, confluence page stub, repo path ops/playbooks/.

Communication and rituals:
- Weekly 30m sync for guardians during pilot phases (strict agenda: signal review, action items, blockers).
- Monthly reliability review with PMs and customer success for outward-facing services.
- Post-incident retrospective within 5 business days, decision log entry within 48 hours.
- Runbook refresh prior to each rollout window.

Measurement and success metrics (what we track):
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM) — target: 30% reduction at 90d vs baseline.
- Error budget burn rate distribution (identify outliers).
- Time from SLO adoption to steady-state (no emergency actions) — target: < 60 days for 50% of services.
- Runbook completeness score (boolean checks).

Risk, open questions, and mitigations:
- Risk: noisy alerts cause guardian fatigue.
  - Mitigation: stricter alert thresholds in pilot + daily noise reviews.
- Risk: PMs push high-risk SLO targets for marketing reasons.
  - Mitigation: require product sign-off and a tradeoff doc with cost estimate for each target.
- Open: how to handle model-quality SLOs (semantic drift) — need research spike with applied-ml to define measurable signals.

Tactical checkboxes (quick wins to start tomorrow):
- [ ] Create slack channel and calendar invite template for guardian sync.
- [ ] Fork runbook template and add to ops/playbooks/.
- [ ] Identify pilot services and schedule baseline metric capture.
- [ ] Open JIRA-RELIAB-1345 (pilot coordination) and assign owners.

Notes to self / workshop fragments:
- Keep SLOs small and focused: availability OR core latency OR inference correctness; avoid doubling up until stabilization.
- Consider a "safe-mode" fallback behavior for inference routes (reduced features, cached responses) when error budget burns fast.
- Investigate an "SLO shadowing" dashboard that overlays candidate SLO on historical traces for quick vetting.

References and links (placeholders):
- Confluence: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=CONFLUENCE-OPS-TRUST-NETWORK-PL
- Jira epic: JIRA-RELIAB-1345
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/4892

Next steps (owner-swimlane):
- Priya: finalize runbook template by 2026-02-18; create slack + calendar.
- Liam: set up pilot dashboards and baseline queries by 2026-02-19.
- Sofia: draft CI gating example and POC play for alert automation by 2026-02-24.
- Devon: draft tabletop scenario and incident script by 2026-02-20.

Unresolved items to bring to the trust network kickoff:
- Are customer-facing quality SLOs governed differently? (CS/legal input)
- How should on-call compensation/rotation adjust for guardian pairs?
- Decision on persistence of CI gating for feature flags (opt-in vs auto-enable).

If you want to iterate: add a short section per pilot service with current baseline numbers and early observations. This doc will be the living coordination artifact while we run the pilots; once stable we’ll transcribe the patterns into a canonical reliability handbook.
